info.title: GitLab REST API
info.description: GitLab REST API used to interact with a GitLab installation.

tags.name: AI Catalog
tags.description:
Use this API to seed the external agents that an instance offers in the
[AI Catalog](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/ai_catalog/).

This endpoint requires administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Access requests
tags.description: Use this API to interact with access requests for groups and projects.

tags.name: Access tokens
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with access tokens including:

- [Personal access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/).
- [Group access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/settings/group_access_tokens/).
- [Project access tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/settings/project_access_tokens/).
- [Impersonation tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/#impersonation-tokens).

tags.name: Active context
tags.description:
Use this API to administer the ActiveContext indexing infrastructure, including its connections,
collection options, the namespaces enabled for code indexing, and the dead queue.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Add on purchases
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve, create, and update the
[subscription add-on](https://docs.gitlab.com/subscriptions/subscription-add-ons/) purchases of a namespace.

tags.name: Advanced search rollout
tags.description:
Use this API to control what percentage of namespaces are indexed for
[advanced search](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/advanced_search/elasticsearch/), rolling
indexing forward or back.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Use this API to retrieve the [GitLab agents for Kubernetes](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/clusters/agent/) that a CI/CD job is authorized to access.

tags.name: Ai agent audit events
tags.description: Operations related to ai agent audit events.

tags.name: Ai agent identities
tags.description:
Use this API to register an external agent identity for a project, so that agent
sessions can be attributed to a user and a machine. Registration returns the existing record if one
already exists, or is rejected if the identity has been revoked.

External agents are published through the
[AI Catalog](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/ai_catalog/), and act with a
[composite identity](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/composite_identity/) that
combines a service account with the human user who initiated the request.

tags.name: Ai agent sessions
tags.description: Operations related to ai agent sessions.

tags.name: Alert management
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with metric images for [alerts](https://docs.gitlab.com/operations/incident_management/alerts/).

Additional endpoints are available with the [GraphQL API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#alertmanagementalert).

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve analytics about a group's activity, a project's deployment frequency, and
product analytics data. For more information about the group metrics, see
[group activity analytics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/manage/#group-activity-analytics).

tags.name: Applications
tags.description:
Use this API to manage instance-wide OAuth applications that:

- [Use GitLab as an authentication provider](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/oauth_provider/).
- [Allow access to GitLab resources on a user's behalf](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/oauth2/).

> [!note]
> You cannot use this API to manage group applications or individual user applications.

tags.name: Approval rules
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the [merge request approval rules](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/approvals/rules/)
defined for a project or a group, where the rules of a group apply to the projects it contains.

All endpoints require authentication. To manage the approval rules of an individual merge request,
use the [merge request approvals API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/merge_request_approvals/).

tags.name: Attestations
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve and download [provenance attestations](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipeline_security/slsa/level_3/provenance_v1/) for a project.

> [!note]
> The availability of these endpoints is controlled by a feature flag. They are available for
> testing, but not ready for production use.

tags.name: Audit events
tags.description:
Use this API to list and retrieve the
[audit events](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/compliance/audit_events/) recorded for an instance or a group.

tags.name: Authn
tags.description: Operations related to authn.

tags.name: Avatars
tags.description: Use this API to retrieve and upload avatars for [users](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/), [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/), and [projects](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/).

tags.name: Award emoji
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [emoji reactions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/emoji_reactions/).

GitLab objects that accept emoji reactions are called awardables.
You can react with emoji on the following resources:

- [Epics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/epics/)
- [Issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/)
- [Merge requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/)
- [Snippets](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/snippets/)
- [Comments](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/emoji_reactions/#emoji-reactions-for-comments)

tags.name: Badges
tags.description:
Use this API to manage badges for [projects](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/badges/) and [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/badges/#group-badges).

## Placeholders

Badges support placeholders that are replaced in real time in both the link and image URL.
The following placeholders are available:

- `%{project_path}`: replaced by the project path.
- `%{project_title}`: replaced by the project title.
- `%{project_name}`: replaced by the project name.
- `%{project_id}`: replaced by the project ID.
- `%{project_namespace}`: replaced by the project's namespace full path.
- `%{group_name}`: replaced by the project's top-level group name.
- `%{gitlab_server}`: replaced by the project's server name.
- `%{gitlab_pages_domain}`: replaced by the domain name hosting GitLab Pages.
- `%{default_branch}`: replaced by the project default branch.
- `%{commit_sha}`: replaced by the project's last commit SHA.
- `%{latest_tag}`: replaced by the project's last tag.

Group badge endpoints operate outside a project's context, so placeholder values are taken from the
group's earliest-created project. If no projects exist in the group, the URL is returned unchanged.

tags.name: Batched background migrations
tags.description:
Use this API to list, retrieve, pause, and resume the
[batched background migrations](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/background_migrations/) running on an instance.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Batched background operations
tags.description:
Use this API to list, retrieve, restart, and stop the batched background operations running on an
instance.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Boards
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [issue boards](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issue_board/) and their lists, for both projects and [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issue_board/#group-issue-boards).

Every call to this API requires authentication. If the project or group is private and the
authenticated user is not a member, a `GET` request results in a `404` status code.

tags.name: Branches
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [Git branches](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/branches/).

To change the branch protections configured for a project, use the [protected branches API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/protected_branches/).

tags.name: Broadcast messages
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with banners and notifications displayed in the UI. For more information, see [broadcast messages](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/broadcast_messages/).

GET requests do not require authentication. All other broadcast message API endpoints are accessible only to administrators. Non-GET requests by:

- Unauthenticated users result in `401 Unauthorized`.
- Authenticated non-administrators result in `403 Forbidden`.

tags.name: CI catalog
tags.description:
Use this API to publish a release of a component project to the
[CI/CD catalog](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/components/).

This endpoint is intended for CLI tooling and must be authenticated with a
[job token](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/ci_job_token/).

tags.name: CI jobs
tags.description: Use this API to interact with [CI/CD jobs](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/).

tags.name: CI lint
tags.description:
Use this API to [validate a GitLab CI/CD configuration](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/yaml/lint/).

These endpoints take JSON-encoded YAML content. To preserve the formatting of your CI/CD
configuration, it can help to escape and encode the YAML with a third-party tool such as
[`jq`](https://jqlang.org/) before you make the request.

tags.name: CI minutes
tags.description:
> [!warning]
> These endpoints are [deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/515371) and were used
> only by the GitLab subscription portal.

Use this API to record a purchase of
[compute minutes](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/compute_minutes/) for a namespace, and to
transfer purchased packs to another namespace.

tags.name: CI resource groups
tags.description: Use this API to interact with [resource groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/resource_groups/).

tags.name: CI runners
tags.description:
> [!warning]
> Registering a runner with a registration token is
> [deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/380872) and disabled by default in
> GitLab 17.0 and later.

Use this API to register a [runner](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/) with an instance, verify its
authentication, reset its authentication token, and unregister it. GitLab Runner uses these endpoints
itself.

To create a runner, or to manage runners that already exist, use the Runners endpoints.

tags.name: CI triggers
tags.description: Use this API to [trigger pipelines](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/triggers/).

tags.name: CI variables
tags.description:
Use this API to manage CI/CD variables for a [project](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/variables/#for-a-project),
a [group](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/variables/#for-a-group), or an
[instance](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/variables/#for-an-instance).

Managing project variables requires the Maintainer role for the project.
Managing group variables requires the Owner role for the group.
Managing instance variables requires administrator access.

tags.name: Cluster agents
tags.description: Use this API to interact with the [GitLab agent for Kubernetes](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/clusters/agent/).

tags.name: Clusters
tags.description:
> [!warning]
> These certificate-based cluster endpoints are [deprecated](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/configure/-/work_items/8).

Use this API to manage and discover the certificate-based Kubernetes clusters of an
[instance](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/instance/clusters/), a
[group](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/clusters/), or a
[project](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/clusters/). Connecting a cluster to a group or an
instance lets you use the same cluster across multiple projects.

Instance endpoints require administrator access. Group and project endpoints require the Maintainer
or Owner role.

tags.name: Code Suggestions
tags.description: Operations related to Code Suggestions.

tags.name: Code review analytics
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve
[code review analytics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/analytics/code_review_analytics/) for a project.

tags.name: Code search
tags.description:
Use this API to administer the [Zoekt](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/zoekt/) nodes that power
[exact code search](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/exact_code_search/), including which
namespaces each node indexes, replica overrides, and triggering indexing for a project.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Commit statuses
tags.description:
Use this API to list the statuses recorded against a
[commit](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/commits/), and to add or update the status
that an external [CI/CD job](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/) reports for a commit.

tags.name: Commits
tags.description: Use this API to manage [Git commits](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/commits/).

tags.name: Compliance policy settings
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the security policy settings for an instance, and to set the status of
compliance controls that are evaluated by an external service.

Managing security policy settings requires administrator access to the instance, and security policies
require the Ultimate tier.
Setting the status of a compliance control requires HMAC, Timestamp, and Nonce authentication.

External controls support periodic ping functionality. When ping is enabled, which is the default,
GitLab resets the control status to `pending` every 12 hours. When ping is disabled, the control
status changes only through API calls.

tags.name: Container registry
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the [GitLab container registry](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/container_registry/):
list the registry repositories in a project or a group, retrieve or delete individual repositories and
their tags, and receive registry events.

To authenticate with these endpoints from a CI/CD job, pass the [`$CI_JOB_TOKEN`](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/ci_job_token/)
variable as the `JOB-TOKEN` header. The job token only has access to the container registry
of the project that created the pipeline.

tags.name: Custom attributes
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the custom attributes set on users, groups, and projects.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: DORA metrics
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve [DORA metrics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/analytics/dora_metrics/) for
groups and projects. Additional metrics are available through the
[GraphQL API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/).

These endpoints require the Reporter, Developer, Maintainer, or Owner role.

tags.name: Data management
tags.description:
> [!note]
> These endpoints are an [experiment](https://docs.gitlab.com/policy/development_stages_support/).

Use this API to inspect and checksum the records that an instance stores for a given model.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Database dictionary
tags.description:
Use this API to list the tables in a GitLab database and retrieve the
[database dictionary](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/database/database_dictionary/) entry for a
single table.

Retrieving the entry for a single table requires administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Dependency firewall
tags.description: Operations related to dependency firewall.

tags.name: Dependency management
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve a project's dependencies and to export
[dependency lists](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/application_security/dependency_list/) for a project,
group, or pipeline.

Every call to these endpoints requires authentication. To retrieve a project's dependencies, the user
must be authorized to read the repository. To see vulnerabilities in a response, the user must also be
authorized to read the [project security dashboard](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/application_security/security_dashboard/).
To create or download a dependency list export, the user must have the `read_dependency` permission,
and exports can be downloaded only by the user who created them.

tags.name: Dependency proxy
tags.description:
Use this API to purge the cache of a group's
[dependency proxy](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/dependency_proxy/).

tags.name: Deploy resources
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [deploy keys](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/deploy_keys/),
[deploy tokens](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/deploy_tokens/), and
[code deployments](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/environments/deployments/) to GitLab environments.

tags.name: Discussions
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [discussions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/discussions/). This includes
[comments, threads](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/discussions/), and system notes about changes to an object
(for example, when a milestone changes).

To manage label notes, use the [resource label events API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/resource_label_events/).

tags.name: Draft notes
tags.description:
Use this API to manage draft notes. These notes are pending, unpublished comments on merge requests.
Draft notes can start a discussion, or continue an existing discussion as a reply.

Before publishing, draft notes are visible only to the author.

tags.name: Duo workflow flow callback hooks
tags.description: Operations related to duo workflow flow callback hooks.

tags.name: Enterprise users
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the [enterprise users](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/enterprise_user/) of a
top-level group, including disabling two-factor authentication for them.

These endpoints work only for top-level groups, and require the Owner role for that group. The users
themselves do not have to be members of the group.

tags.name: Environments
tags.description: Use this API to interact with [GitLab environments](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/environments/).

tags.name: Epics
tags.description:
> [!warning]
> The Epics REST API was [deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/460668) in GitLab 17.0
> and is planned for removal in v5 of the API. From GitLab 17.4 to 18.0, if
> [the new look for epics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/epics/#epics-as-work-items) is enabled,
> or in GitLab 18.1 and later, use the Work Items API instead. For more information, see
> [migrate epic APIs to work items](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/epic_work_items_api_migration_guide/).
> This change is a breaking change.

Use this API to manage [epics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/epics/), the issues assigned to
them, their child and [related epics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/epics/linked_epics/), and
[group epic boards](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/epics/epic_boards/).

Every call to this API must be authenticated. If a user is not a member of a private group, a `GET`
request on that group results in a `404` status code.

Epics are available only in GitLab [Premium and Ultimate](https://about.gitlab.com/pricing/). If the
Epics or Related Epics feature is not available, a `403` status code is returned.

tags.name: Error tracking
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [error tracking](https://docs.gitlab.com/operations/error_tracking/) settings
and client keys for a project.

These endpoints require the Maintainer or Owner role.

tags.name: Events
tags.description:
Use this API to review event activity for a user, a project, or an instance. Events cover a wide
range of actions, such as joining a project, commenting on an issue, pushing changes to a merge
request, or closing an epic.

Activity is subject to retention limits. For more information, see the
[user activity time period limit](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/contributions_calendar/#event-time-period-limit)
and the [project activity time period limit](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/working_with_projects/#view-project-activity).

These endpoints have some limitations:

- Some epic features, such as child items, linked items, start dates, due dates, and health statuses, are not returned.
- Some merge request notes use the `DiscussionNote` type instead, which is [not supported](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/discussions/#understand-note-types-in-the-api).
- Bulk push events, created when a push exceeds the [push event activities limit](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/settings/push_event_activities_limit/), are returned with limited details.

tags.name: Experiments
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve the A/B experiments running on an instance. This API is for internal use
only, requires you to be a [GitLab team member](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/-/group_members),
and cannot be used with anonymous or unauthenticated users. For experiments involving anonymous users,
use the [`glex_force` query parameter](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/experiment_guide/implementing_experiments/#client-side-glex_force-query-parameter)
instead.

tags.name: External status checks
tags.description: Use this API to manage [external status checks](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/status_checks/).

tags.name: Feature flags
tags.description:
Use this API to manage a project's [feature flags](https://docs.gitlab.com/operations/feature_flags/)
and the [user lists](https://docs.gitlab.com/operations/feature_flags/#user-list) that scope them to
particular users.

These endpoints require the Developer, Maintainer, or Owner role.

tags.name: Features
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the Flipper-based feature flags used in the development of GitLab itself.

These endpoints support only boolean and percentage-of-time gate values, and require administrator
authorization.

tags.name: Files
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [repository files](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/).
You can also [configure rate limits](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/settings/files_api_rate_limits/)
for this API.

tags.name: Freeze periods
tags.description: Use this API to interact with deployment [freeze periods](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/releases/#prevent-unintentional-releases-by-setting-a-deploy-freeze).

tags.name: GLQL
tags.description:
Use this API to execute [GitLab Query Language (GLQL)](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/glql/) queries
programmatically. GLQL provides a simplified query language to search and filter
[GitLab resources](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/glql/#supported-areas) such as issues, merge requests,
and epics across projects and groups.

The group or project must allow access to its data. For private groups and projects, you must
authenticate with a [personal access token](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/)
that has the appropriate permissions.

tags.name: Geo
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [Geo sites](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/geo/). All of these
endpoints require administrator access.

> [!warning]
> The Geo Nodes endpoints are [deprecated](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/369140) and
> are planned for removal in v5 of the API. Use the
> [Geo Sites API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/geo_sites/) instead. This change is a breaking change.

tags.name: GitLab Duo
tags.description:
Use this API to generate responses for [GitLab Duo Chat](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/gitlab_duo_chat/)
and other GitLab Duo features.

On GitLab.com, these endpoints are for internal use only. On GitLab Self-Managed, you can enable them
[with a feature flag](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/feature_flags/) named `access_rest_chat`.
You must be a [GitLab team member](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/-/group_members) to use these endpoints.

tags.name: GitLab Duo workflows
tags.description:
Use this API to create and manage [flows](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/flows/) in the
[GitLab Duo Agent Platform](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/).
Flows are combinations of AI agents that work together to complete developer tasks,
such as fixing bugs, writing code, or resolving vulnerabilities.

tags.name: GitLab Pages
tags.description:
Use this API to [administer](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/pages/) and
[use](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/pages/) GitLab Pages, including managing
[custom domains](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/pages/custom_domains_ssl_tls_certification/).

GitLab Pages must be enabled to use these endpoints.

tags.name: GitLab subscriptions
tags.description:
Use this API to create and update the [subscription](https://docs.gitlab.com/subscriptions/) attached
to a namespace.

tags.name: Group credentials inventory
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the credentials that members of a top-level group hold, including their
personal access tokens, resource access tokens, and SSH keys. You can list these credentials, revoke
them, and rotate the tokens. For more information, see
[credentials inventory](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/credentials_inventory/).

tags.name: Group import and export
tags.description:
Use this API to [migrate a group structure](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/import/) by exporting
and importing a file. When you use it with the
[project import and export API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/project_import_export/), you can
preserve relationships that span the group, such as connections between project issues and group
epics. Run the group export and import first, then import the project exports into the group
structure.

A group export includes group milestones, boards, labels, badges, members, events, wikis (Premium
and Ultimate only), and subgroups. Each subgroup includes all of the same data.

To preserve the member list and permissions of an imported group, make sure those users exist on the
destination instance before you import.

Because of [issue 405168](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/405168), imported groups have
a `private` visibility level unless you import them into a parent group. By default, groups imported
into a parent group inherit the visibility of the parent.

The destination instance uses the group relations export endpoints during
[group migration by direct transfer](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/import/). You don't
usually need to call them yourself. In this context, a relation is an exportable item such as an
epic, including any related items such as a label. These endpoints require your instance to meet certain
[prerequisites](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/import/direct_transfer_migrations/#prerequisites),
and can't be used with the file-based export and import endpoints.

tags.name: Groups
tags.description:
Use this API to view and manage [groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/) and the resources they contain, including:

- Group settings, members, and security settings.
- [Group issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/) and issue statistics.
- [Markdown uploads](https://docs.gitlab.com/security/user_file_uploads/) referenced in epics or wiki pages.
- Bulk [reassignment of placeholder users](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/import/mapping/reassignment/#request-reassignment-by-using-a-csv-file) after an import.

Endpoint responses might vary based on the [permissions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/permissions/)
of the authenticated user in the group. If a user isn't a member of a private group, requests to
that group return a `404 Not Found` status code.

For project members, use the [project members API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/project_members/).

tags.name: Hooks
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the hooks that GitLab uses to notify external services about events:

- [Project webhooks](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/integrations/webhooks/) are limited to a single project.
- [Group webhooks](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/integrations/webhooks/#group-webhooks) apply to all projects and subgroups in a group.
- [System hooks](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/system_hooks/) apply to the entire instance.

You can also test a hook, inspect its event log, resend an event, and manage its custom headers and
URL variables.

Managing project webhooks requires administrator access or the Maintainer or Owner role for the
project. Managing group webhooks requires administrator access or the Owner role for the group.
Managing system hooks requires administrator access.

tags.name: Imports
tags.description:
Use this API to migrate groups and projects by using
[direct transfer](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/import/direct_transfer_migrations/), and to
[import repositories from external sources](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/import/).

Before migrating by direct transfer, see the
[prerequisites](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/import/direct_transfer_migrations/#prerequisites).

> [!note]
> User contribution mapping is not supported when you import projects to a
> [personal namespace](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/namespace/#types-of-namespaces). All
> contributions are assigned to the personal namespace owner and cannot be reassigned.

tags.name: Instance
tags.description:
Use this API to manage an instance's
[appearance](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/appearance/) and
[application settings](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/settings/#available-settings), and to retrieve
statistics about the instance.

Changes to application settings are subject to caching and might not take effect immediately. By
default, GitLab caches application settings for 60 seconds. For more information, see
[application cache interval](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/application_settings_cache/).

All of these endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [integrations](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/integrations/) for a
project, or for a group and its subgroups.

Managing integrations requires the Maintainer or Owner role for the project or group.

tags.name: Internal operations
tags.description: Operations related to internal operations.

tags.name: Invitations
tags.description: Use this API to manage invitations and add users to a [group](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/#add-users-to-a-group) or [project](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/members/).

tags.name: Issues
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/), their
[links to related issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/related_issues/), and issue
statistics. You can:

- Create, update, and delete issues.
- Manage issue metadata, like assignees, labels, milestones, and time tracking.
- Cross-reference issues and merge requests.
- Track issue movement and promotion between projects and epics.
- Retrieve statistics about issues.

If a user is not a member of a private project, a `GET` request on that project results in a `404`
status code.

> [!note]
> The `references.relative` attribute is relative to the group or project of the issue being requested.
> When an issue is fetched from its project, the `relative` format is the same as the `short` format.
> When requested across groups or projects, it's expected to be the same as the `full` format.

tags.name: Iterations
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve [iterations](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/iterations/) for a group or
a project.

Projects no longer have their own iterations, but you can use the project endpoint to retrieve the
iterations of a project's ancestor groups.

tags.name: Jira Connect subscriptions
tags.description:
Use this API to subscribe a namespace to an installation of the
[GitLab for Jira Cloud app](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/jira/connect-app/).

tags.name: Jira forge installation
tags.description:
Use this API to configure a GitLab for Jira (Forge) installation, by setting the GitLab instance URL
it points to and registering the system token it uses to synchronize development information. For more
information, see the [Jira integrations](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/jira/).

tags.name: Jira forge subscriptions
tags.description:
Use this API to list, create, and delete the namespace subscriptions of a GitLab for Jira (Forge)
installation. For more information, see the [Jira integrations](https://docs.gitlab.com/integration/jira/).

tags.name: Job artifacts
tags.description: Use this API to download, keep, and delete [job artifacts](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/job_artifacts/).

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description:
Use this API to run CI/CD jobs on a [runner](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/): request the next
job, update its state, append to its log, and transfer its artifacts.

GitLab Runner uses these endpoints itself.

tags.name: Keys
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve information about [SSH keys](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/ssh/), manage a
user's SSH and [GPG keys](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/signed_commits/gpg/),
and manage [SSH certificates for top-level groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/ssh_certificates/).

Queries about deploy key fingerprints also retrieve information about the projects using that key.
If you use a SHA256 fingerprint in an API call, URL-encode the fingerprint.

Managing group SSH certificates requires the Owner role for a top-level group.

tags.name: Knowledge graph
tags.description:
Use this API to list the namespaces enabled for the knowledge graph, and to enable or disable an
individual namespace.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: LDAP
tags.description:
Use this API to search the LDAP groups available to an instance, and to
[manage group memberships with LDAP](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/access_and_permissions/#manage-group-memberships-with-ldap)
by managing a group's LDAP links and triggering an LDAP synchronization.

tags.name: Labels
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [labels](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/labels/) for both projects and
groups. For the difference between the two, see
[types of labels](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/labels/#types-of-labels).

tags.name: Licenses
tags.description:
Use this API to add, retrieve, and delete the license that
[activates GitLab Enterprise Edition](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/license_file/).

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: Use this API to connect Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients to the GitLab MCP server.

tags.name: ML Model Registry
tags.description:
Use this API to upload and download the files attached to a version of a machine learning model in
the [model registry](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/ml/model_registry/). To create models and model
versions, use an [MLflow client](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/ml/experiment_tracking/mlflow_client/).

tags.name: MLOps
tags.description:
Use this API to track machine learning experiments, runs, and metrics, and to manage the
[model registry](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/ml/model_registry/). These endpoints implement
the MLflow REST API, so you can point an
[MLflow client](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/ml/experiment_tracking/mlflow_client/) at GitLab.

tags.name: Markdown
tags.description:
Use this API to render [Markdown](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/markdown/) content as HTML.

All requests to this API must be [authenticated](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/).

> [!note]
> The availability of this feature is controlled by a feature flag.
> This feature is available for testing, but not ready for production use.

tags.name: Member roles
tags.description: Use this API to interact with member roles for your GitLab.com groups or entire GitLab Self-Managed instance.

tags.name: Members
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the [members](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/members/) of a group or a
project, including inherited memberships, membership approvals, and the billable members of a group.

tags.name: Merge request approvals
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [merge request approvals](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/approvals/)
and the group and project [approval settings](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/approvals/settings/)
that govern them. All endpoints require authentication.

Endpoints to approve, unapprove, reset approvals, and retrieve approval state are available on all
tiers, including Free. All other endpoints require Premium or Ultimate, and each one shows its tier.

> [!note]
> The `merge_request_iid` and `id` path parameters must each be a single value.
> Passing multiple space-separated values (for example, `451 454 458`) is not
> supported and returns `400 Bad Request`. To act on multiple merge requests,
> make one request per merge request IID.

tags.name: Merge requests
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [merge requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/) in a
project, and to list the merge requests across a group or an entire instance. You can:

- Automate any part of the code review process.
- Connect code changes to external tools.
- Send merge request information to non-GitLab systems in your preferred format.
- Update, approve, merge, or block merge requests based on data from external systems.
- Add [commits from previous merge requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/commits/#show-commits-from-previous-merge-requests) to a merge request for more context.

All API calls to non-public information require authentication.

tags.name: Merge trains
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve the [merge trains](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/merge_trains/) of a
project. These endpoints require the Developer, Maintainer, or Owner role, and support
[offset-based pagination](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/#offset-based-pagination).

Each object in a response represents one merge request in a train, not an entire train. Requesting
merge trains without a target branch can return entries from more than one train in the project.

Responses do not include an explicit queue position, and return merge requests as a flat list rather
than grouped by train:

- For an exact queue position, sort by `id` in ascending order, or use the GraphQL API
  [`MergeTrainCar.index`](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#mergetraincar-index) field.
- To group merge requests by train, use the `target_branch` attribute, or query the GraphQL API
  [`Project.mergeTrains`](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#projectmergetrains) and
  [`MergeTrain.cars`](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#mergetraincars) fields.

tags.name: Metadata
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve metadata about a GitLab instance, including its version, its revision,
whether it is Enterprise Edition, and the configuration of the
[GitLab agent server for Kubernetes (KAS)](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/clusters/kas/).

tags.name: Metric images
tags.description:
Use this API to upload, list, update, and delete the metric images attached to an issue, such as the
charts attached to an [incident](https://docs.gitlab.com/operations/incident_management/incidents/).

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve the definitions of the metrics that GitLab collects for
[Service Ping](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/internal_analytics/service_ping/).

tags.name: Migrations
tags.description:
Use this API to mark GitLab database migrations as successful, so that a deployment can proceed
without re-running them.

These endpoints are available for GitLab Self-Managed and require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Milestones
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [milestones](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/milestones/) for both
projects and groups.

tags.name: Mobile push subscriptions
tags.description: Operations related to mobile push subscriptions.

tags.name: Namespace projects
tags.description: Operations related to namespace projects.

tags.name: Namespaces
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with namespaces, a special resource category used to organize users and groups. For more information, see [namespaces](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/namespace/).

This API uses [pagination](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/#pagination) to filter results.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the comments and system records attached to GitLab content. You can:

- Create and modify comments on issues, merge requests, epics, snippets, commits, and wiki pages.
- Retrieve [system-generated notes](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/system_notes/) about object changes.
- Control visibility with confidential and internal flags.

Some system-generated notes are tracked as separate resource events instead, including
[label](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/resource_label_events/),
[state](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/resource_state_events/),
[milestone](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/resource_milestone_events/),
[weight](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/resource_weight_events/), and
[iteration](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/resource_iteration_events/) events.

By default, `GET` requests return 20 results at a time, because the results are
[paginated](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/#pagination).

tags.name: Notification settings
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve and update [notification settings](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/notifications/)
globally for your account, or for an individual group or project, which overrides the global setting.

tags.name: OAuth applications
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve the server configuration that the workspaces agent requires.

This endpoint is internal and used by GitLab components.

tags.name: Offline transfers
tags.description:
Use this API to start and track offline transfer exports and imports, which migrate data between
GitLab instances that cannot reach each other over a network.

tags.name: Orbit
tags.description:
Use this API to serve repository and merge request content to
[GitLab Orbit](https://docs.gitlab.com/orbit/), which indexes a group's software development
lifecycle into a queryable knowledge graph. These endpoints expose project metadata, commits, changed
paths, blobs, repository archives, and merge request diffs, and redact sensitive values from the
content Orbit ingests.

These endpoints are internal and used by the GitLab Orbit service.

> [!note]
> The availability of these endpoints is controlled by a feature flag, and GitLab Orbit is in beta.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: Use this API to interact with GitLab organizations. For more information, see [organizations](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/organization/).

tags.name: Packages
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the [packages](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/package_registry/) stored
in a project or a group.

tags.name: Packages: Cargo
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with the Cargo package registry, including its sparse index, registry
configuration, and crate downloads. Generally these endpoints are used by Cargo itself and are not
meant for manual consumption. For more information, see the
[package registry](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/package_registry/).

tags.name: Packages: Composer
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with the [Composer package manager client](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/composer_repository/).

> [!warning]
> This API is used by the [Composer package manager client](https://getcomposer.org/)
> and is generally not meant for manual consumption.

These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods.
See the [Composer package registry documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/composer_repository/)
for details on which headers and token types are supported. Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

tags.name: Packages: Conan
tags.description:
> [!warning]
> The Conan registry is not FIPS compliant and is disabled when FIPS mode is enabled. These
> endpoints all return `404 Not Found`.

Use this API to interact with the Conan package manager for
[v1](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/conan_1_repository/) and
[v2](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/conan_2_repository/) repositories. The v1 endpoints work
for both projects and instances, and the availability of the v2 endpoints is controlled by a feature
flag. Generally these endpoints are used by the Conan package manager client and are not meant for
manual consumption.

> [!note]
> These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods. See each route for
> details on how credentials are expected to be passed. Undocumented authentication methods might be
> removed in the future.

tags.name: Packages: Debian
tags.description:
> [!warning]
> These endpoints are under development and are not ready for production use due to limited
> functionality. The package endpoints are used by Debian package clients such as
> [dput](https://manpages.debian.org/stable/dput-ng/dput.1.en.html) and
> [apt-get](https://manpages.debian.org/stable/apt/apt-get.8.en.html), and are generally not meant
> for manual consumption.

Use this API to manage [Debian distributions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/debian_repository/)
for groups and projects, and to publish and retrieve Debian packages. The distribution endpoints are
behind a feature flag that is disabled by default. To use them, enable the
[group](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/packages/debian_group_distributions/#enable-the-debian-group-api) or
[project](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/packages/debian_project_distributions/#enable-the-debian-api)
Debian API.

> [!note]
> These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods. For the supported headers
> and token types, see the [Debian registry documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/debian_repository/).
> Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

tags.name: Packages: Helm
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with [Helm package clients](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/helm_repository/).

> [!warning]
> This API is used by the Helm-related package clients such as [Helm](https://helm.sh/)
> and [`helm-push`](https://github.com/chartmuseum/helm-push/#readme),
> and is generally not meant for manual consumption.

These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods.
See the [Helm registry documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/helm_repository/)
for details on which headers and token types are supported. Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

tags.name: Packages: NPM
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with the [npm package manager client](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/npm_registry/).

> [!warning]
> This API is used by the [npm package manager client](https://docs.npmjs.com/)
> and is not meant for manual consumption.

These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods.
See the [npm package registry documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/npm_registry/)
for details on which headers and token types are supported. Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

tags.name: Packages: NuGet
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with the [NuGet package manager client](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/nuget_repository/).

> [!warning]
> This API is used by the [NuGet package manager client](https://www.nuget.org/)
> and is generally not meant for manual consumption.

These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods.
See the [NuGet package registry documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/nuget_repository/)
for details on which headers and token types are supported. Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

tags.name: Packages: PyPi
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with the [PyPI package manager client](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/pypi_repository/).

> [!warning]
> This API is used by the [PyPI package manager client](https://pypi.org/)
> and is generally not meant for manual consumption.

These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods.
See the [PyPI package registry documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/pypi_repository/)
for details on which headers and token types are supported. Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

> [!note]
> [Twine 3.4.2](https://twine.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html?highlight=FIPS#id28) or greater
> is recommended when FIPS mode is enabled.

tags.name: Packages: RPM
tags.description:
Use this API to upload RPM packages to the
[package registry](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/package_registry/).

tags.name: Packages: RubyGem
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with the [Ruby gems and Bundler package manager clients](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/rubygems_registry/).

> [!warning]
> This API is used by the Ruby gems and Bundler package manager clients and is generally not meant
> for manual consumption. This API is under development and is not ready for production use due to
> limited functionality.

These endpoints do not adhere to the standard API authentication methods.
See the [Ruby gems registry documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/rubygems_registry/)
for details on which headers and token types are supported. Undocumented authentication methods might be removed in the future.

tags.name: Pipeline schedules
tags.description: Use this API to interact with [pipeline schedules](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/schedules/).

tags.name: Pipelines
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [CI/CD pipelines](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/) and the
[jobs](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/) they run.

tags.name: Plan limits
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve and change the application limits of a subscription plan.

The available plans depend on the GitLab edition. In the Community Edition, only the `default` plan
exists. The Enterprise Edition has additional plans.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Policy store
tags.description: Operations related to policy store.

tags.name: Project Google Cloud integration
tags.description: Use this API to interact with the Google Cloud integration. For more information, see [GitLab and Google Cloud integration](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/gitlab_google_cloud_integration/).

tags.name: Project alias
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [project aliases](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/working_with_projects/#project-aliases).
After you create an alias for a project, users can clone the repository with that alias, which can be
helpful when migrating repositories.

All endpoints require administrator authorization.

tags.name: Project approvals
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve and change a project's
[merge request approval configuration](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/merge_requests/approvals/settings/),
such as the number of approvals a merge request requires.

All endpoints require authentication.

tags.name: Project import
tags.description:
Use this API to [import repositories from external sources](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/import/)
and to [migrate a project](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/settings/import_export/) between
GitLab instances.

If you first migrate the parent group structure with the
[group import and export API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/group_import_export/), you can preserve
relationships that span the group, such as connections between project issues and group epics.
After an import, use the [project-level CI/CD variables API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/project_level_variables/)
to restore CI/CD variables. You must still migrate your
[container registry](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/container_registry/) over a series of
Docker pulls and pushes, and re-run any CI/CD pipelines to retrieve build artifacts.

The project relations export endpoints are used by the destination instance during
[group migration by direct transfer](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/import/) to migrate a
project structure, and you don't usually need to call them yourself. In this context, a relation is
an exportable item such as a merge request, including any related items such as a label.

> [!note]
> User contribution mapping is not supported when you import projects to a
> [personal namespace](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/namespace/#types-of-namespaces). All
> contributions are assigned to the personal namespace owner and cannot be reassigned.

tags.name: Project mirrors
tags.description: Use this API to manage project [pull mirroring](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/mirror/pull/).

tags.name: Project snapshots
tags.description:
Use this API to download a snapshot of a project's repository, for use in salvaging a corrupt
repository.

These endpoints require administrator access to the instance.

tags.name: Project templates
tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve project-specific templates, in addition to the templates common to the
entire instance:

- [Dockerfile templates](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/templates/dockerfiles/)
- [Gitignore templates](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/templates/gitignores/)
- [GitLab CI/CD configuration templates](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/templates/gitlab_ci_ymls/)
- [Open source license templates](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/templates/licenses/)
- [Issue and merge request templates](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/description_templates/)

These endpoints supersede the instance template endpoints, which are scheduled for removal
in API version 5. [File templates for groups](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/manage/#group-file-templates)
are also supported.

tags.name: Project topics
tags.description: Use this API to interact with project topics. For more information, see [project topics](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/project_topics/).

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [projects](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/) and the resources they contain, including:

- Project settings, visibility, access permissions, and security settings.
- Archiving, transferring, [forking](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/forking_workflow/), and [starring](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/working_with_projects/) projects.
- Project [issues](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/issues/), issue statistics, and project statistics.
- [Markdown uploads](https://docs.gitlab.com/security/user_file_uploads/) referenced in issues, merge requests, snippets, or wiki pages.
- Protection rules for [container image tags](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/container_registry/protected_container_tags/), container repositories, and [packages](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/package_registry/package_protection_rules/).

If a user is not a member of a private project, a `GET` request on that project results in a
`404` status code.

tags.name: Projects job token scope
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with [CI/CD job token](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/jobs/ci_job_token/) scopes.

> [!note]
> All requests to the CI/CD job token scope API endpoint must be [authenticated](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/).
> The authenticated user must have the Maintainer or Owner role for the project.

tags.name: Protected branches
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [protected branches](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/branches/protected/)
for a project, and the [protected branch settings](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/branches/protected/#in-a-group)
that all projects in a group inherit.

GitLab Premium and GitLab Ultimate support more granular protections for pushing to branches.
Administrators can grant permission to modify and push to protected branches only to deploy keys,
instead of specific users.

> [!warning]
> Group protected branch settings are restricted to top-level groups. They support only
> [valid access levels](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/group_protected_branches/#valid-access-levels),
> and cannot name individual users or groups.

tags.name: Protected environments
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [protected environments](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/environments/protected_environments/)
for a project, and [protected environments for a group](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/environments/protected_environments/#protected-environments-for-groups)
for a group.

> [!note]
> The project endpoints require CI/CD to be turned on for the project. If
> [CI/CD is turned off](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/settings/#turn-off-cicd-for-a-project),
> requests return `403 Forbidden`, even for users who otherwise have permission to manage protected
> environments.

tags.name: Protected tags
tags.description: Use this API to manage [protected tags](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/protected_tags/).

tags.name: Provider identities
tags.description:
Use this API to manage the SAML and SCIM identities linked to users in a group.

Prerequisites for the SCIM endpoints:

- You must enable [group SSO](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/saml_sso/).
- You must enable [SCIM for group SSO](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/saml_sso/scim_setup/).
- You must authenticate with a [personal access token](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/)
  or [group access token](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/settings/group_access_tokens/) that has the correct scope.

These endpoints get, check, update, and delete SCIM identities in groups, and do not implement
the [RFC7644 protocol](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7644). They differ from the
[internal group SCIM API](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/internal_api/#group-scim-api) and the
[internal instance SCIM API](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/internal_api/#instance-scim-api),
which implement RFC7644 for SCIM provider integration and require a SCIM token.

tags.name: Push rules
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [push rules](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/push_rules/) for
a project, and [group push rules](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/push_rules/#group-push-rules)
that apply to newly created projects in a group.

Managing group push rules requires the Owner role for the group, or administrator access to the
instance.

> [!note]
> GitLab uses [RE2 syntax](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax) for all regular expressions in push rules.

tags.name: Releases
tags.description:
Use this API to manage [releases](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/releases/) for a project,

- Milestone events record milestone changes for issues and merge requests.
- State events record state changes for issues, merge requests, and epics.
- Weight events record weight changes for issues.

State events do not track the initial state (`created` or `opened`) of a resource. For a resource
that was never closed or reopened, an empty list is returned.

Some scopes are available for [basic search](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/#available-scopes).
When [advanced search](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/advanced_search/#available-scopes) or
[exact code search](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/search/exact_code_search/#available-scopes) is

tags.name: Security scans

[SAST](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/application_security/sast/) results in real time.

tags.name: Service accounts
tags.description:
Use this API to interact with [service accounts](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/service_accounts/).

The number of service accounts you can create depends on your subscription and offering:

- On GitLab Premium and Ultimate, you can create an unlimited number of service accounts for all offerings.
- On GitLab Free, limits vary by offering:
  - For GitLab.com, you can create up to 100 service accounts for each top-level group.
    This includes service accounts created in subgroups or projects.
  - For GitLab Self-Managed, you can create up to 100 service accounts for the entire instance.
    This includes service accounts created for the instance, a group, or a project.

You can also interact with service accounts through the [users API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/users/).
To manage SSH keys for service accounts, use the [user SSH and GPG keys API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/user_keys/).

and processes, and to delete jobs from a queue.

tags.name: Snippets
tags.description:

To move snippets between storages, use the
[snippet repository storage moves API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/snippet_repository_storage_moves/).

scan that already exists for the same SBOM.

tags.name: Storage moves
tags.description:
Use this API to schedule and track [repository storage moves](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/operations/moving_repositories/)
for groups, projects, and snippets. Project moves cover wiki and design repositories, and group
moves cover [group wikis](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/wiki/group/). Moving repositories
can help you [migrate to Gitaly Cluster (Praefect)](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/gitaly/praefect/#migrate-to-gitaly-cluster-praefect).

To ensure data integrity, GitLab places the group, project, or snippet in a temporary read-only
state for the duration of the move. During this time, users receive this message if they try to
push new commits:

```plaintext
The repository is temporarily read-only. Please try again later.
```

This API requires you to [authenticate yourself](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/) as an administrator.

## States

As GitLab processes a storage move, it transitions through different states. Values of `state` are:

- `initial`: The record has been created, but the background job has not yet been scheduled.
- `scheduled`: The background job has been scheduled.
- `started`: The repositories are being copied to the destination storage.
- `replicated`: The repositories have been moved.
- `failed`: The repositories failed to copy, or the checksums did not match.
- `finished`: The repositories have been moved, and the repositories on the source storage have been deleted.
- `cleanup failed`: The repositories have been moved, but the repositories on the source storage could not be deleted.

Suggestions provide a way to propose specific changes that can be directly applied to the code.
You can programmatically create and apply code suggestions in merge request discussions with
this API. Every API call to suggestions must be authenticated.

signature information from signed tags.

tags.description:
Use this API to retrieve the file templates available to an entire instance:

- [Dockerfile templates](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-foss/-/tree/master/vendor/Dockerfile)
- [`.gitignore` templates](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore)
- [CI/CD configuration templates](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/lib/gitlab/ci/templates)
- [Open source license templates](https://choosealicense.com/)

Custom CI/CD templates are not available from these endpoints. For templates specific to a project,
use the [project templates API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/project_templates/).

[project and group visibility](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/public_access/).

audience.

Unleash-compatible client, and to register that client and receive its metrics. Generally these
endpoints are used by an Unleash client and are not meant for manual consumption.

[Service Ping](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/internal_analytics/service_ping/) payload that

tags.name: Users

[your account](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/), manage
[accounts for other users](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/administer_users/),
[moderate user accounts](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/moderate_users/),
[perform follower actions](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/#follow-users), and
[interact with email addresses for user accounts](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/).

them between VS Code and the [Web IDE](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/web_ide/).

tags.description:

[virtual registries](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/virtual_registry/) of a group, along with
the [upstream registries](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/virtual_registry/#manage-upstream-registries)

tags.name: Vulnerabilities
tags.description:
> [!warning]
> These endpoints are in the process of being deprecated and are considered unstable.
> The response payload may be subject to change or breakage across GitLab releases. Use the
> [GraphQL API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#queryvulnerabilities) instead.
> For more information, see [replace vulnerability REST API with GraphQL](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/vulnerabilities/#replace-vulnerability-rest-api-with-graphql).

Use this API to manage [vulnerabilities](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/application_security/vulnerabilities/),
retrieve vulnerability findings, and export [vulnerability reports](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/application_security/vulnerability_report/)
for a project, group, or instance.

Every call to these endpoints must be [authenticated](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/).
If a user isn't a member of a private project, requests return a `404 Not Found` status code. If a
user does not have permission to [view the vulnerability report](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/permissions/#project-application-security),
requests return a `403 Forbidden` status code.

> [!note]
> The former Vulnerabilities API was renamed to the Vulnerability Findings API, and the
> Vulnerabilities name now serves [vulnerability objects](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/13561).
> To fix a broken integration with the former API, change the `vulnerabilities` URL part to
> `vulnerability_findings`.

[web editor](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/repository/web_editor/).

An API for [project wikis](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/wikis/) is also available.

Comments on a wiki page are called `notes`. To interact with them, use the [notes API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/notes/#group-wikis).

tags.name: Work items
tags.description:

or a namespace. Work items are the core elements for planning and tracking work, and cover
[types](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/work_items/#work-item-types) such as issues, tasks, and epics.

Alongside the work items themselves, you can retrieve their children, linked items, linked resources,
notes, discussions, emoji reactions, email participants, and the current user's to-do items.
